title: Simpson’s paradox in win rates
objective: Learners see how Team A can win more often than Team B in every deal size yet have a worse overall win rate, because overall rates are averages weighted by each team’s mix of easy and hard deals.

recommended.why: A custom annotated story can split each overall bar into its deal-size segments, with bar widths showing the mix, so learners watch the weighted average form.

alternative.why: A custom annotated story versus standard grouped bars: which makes the paradox click?

assumptions: Deal counts and win rates are illustrative synthetic numbers, not real sales data
Each team works 200 deals; Team B’s mix is fixed at 25% large deals
Underlying win rates: Team A 78% small and 36% large, Team B 72% small and 28% large; wins are rounded to whole deals
Large deals are harder to win for both teams
units: win rate: percent of deals won
mix: percent of a team’s deals that are large

params.label: Team A's share of large deals

checkDescription: Team A beats Team B within each deal size, and each team's overall win rate equals the mix-weighted average of its segment rates; at the default mix Team A loses overall.

learnerPrompts.predict: Team A wins more small deals and more large deals than Team B. Before you play: must Team A have the higher overall win rate?
learnerPrompts.explain: Drag Team A's share of large deals down until the paradox disappears. Why does the mix alone flip the overall winner?
